Source states: 'Prior to April 2010, when a cholera outbreak emerged in Karamoja, the region had not reported cases of the disease since 1997'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. SUB-NATIONAL absence, Karamoja sub-region, from the peer-reviewed investigation of the April-July 2010 Karamoja outbreak (Cummings et al. 2012 Epidemiol Infect 140(8):1376-1385). The paper names the seven Karamoja districts as Kotido, Nakapiripirit, Abim, Amudat, Napak, Kaabong and Moroto; Amudat, Napak (both 2010), Abim (2006), Kaabong (2005) and Nabilatuk (2017) were carved out of Moroto, Kotido and Nakapiripirit during or after the absence period, so the absence is recorded against the three parent districts that existed throughout and geographically covered the whole sub-region. Supporting context from the same paper: 'information regarding epidemiological trends and location-specific risk factors was not readily available' because of the extended time between outbreaks. This is a SUB-NATIONAL row only; Uganda as a whole reported cholera nationally in every year of 1998-2010, so this row must never be read as a national zero. py/build_weekly_timeseries.py uses national rows only for Uganda, which has ample national coverage, so these rows cannot leak into the national series. source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record Cholera in 1983 annual notification table
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1983-01-01..1983-12-31. Source states: 'Table 1 Cases of Cholera Notified to WHO, 1983'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record annual cholera article for 1983, published 11 May 1984. The African section of the notification table lists only: Algeria, Burundi, Cameroon, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa and the United Republic of Tanzania. Uganda does not appear, i.e. Uganda notified zero cholera cases to WHO for 1983. Control validation of this method: Uganda appears by name in the African section of the same WER annual notification tables for every year it did notify - 1975 (3 cases), 1978 (1120), 1980 (1539), 1987 (140) and 1991 (279 cases and 28 deaths) - so its absence from this year's table is a positive signal of zero notification rather than a text-extraction artefact. Corroboration: Wamala et al. 2013 PLOS NTD state that 'During the subsequent years up to 1993, Uganda reported cholera cases every 2-4 years', describing an episodic epidemic pattern with genuinely quiet intervals. CAVEAT: classified Inferred_Absence rather than Documented_Absence and weighted 0.7 because zero notification under the International Health Regulations is not identical to zero transmission; the WER annual articles of this era themselves warn that there is 'strong reason to believe that cholera is present in a number of countries which have not notified cases in accordance with the International Health Regulations'. Country context: Uganda was in the Ugandan Bush War (1981-1986) in this period, so under-ascertainment is plausible. However Uganda notified cholera to WHO in 1980 (1539 cases), 1982 (190 cases) and 1987 (140 cases), so the WHO notification channel was functioning across the interval. [AGENT 7 REVISION 2026-09-19] AGENT 7 NARROWING: TL moved from 1983-01-01 to 1983-03-25. Uganda's cholera-infected districts were on WHO's infected-areas list as at 27 January and 24 February 1983 and were struck off in the entry 'Areas Removed from the Infected Area List between 18 and 24 March 1983 ... UGANDA - OUGANDA Eastern Province Bugishu District Bukedi (Tororo) District Busoga D.: Mbale Municipality Sebei (Kapchorwa) District Teso (Kumi) District Northern Province Gulu District Kitgum District North Karamoja District'. From 1 January to 24 March 1983 Uganda was formally a cholera-infected country, so only 25 March onward can be asserted as absence. Uganda then does not reappear on the cholera infected-areas list for the rest of the decade, and its 1983 notifiable-disease return was filed and included an explicit reported ZERO for diphtheria, the strongest single indication that Uganda's annual returns were live that year. The January-March portion is recorded in data/UGA/cholera_presence_ai.csv. (reason: Uganda's areas were removed from WHO's cholera infected list on 24 March 1983, so only the remainder of the year can be asserted (Agents 3, 4 and 5 concur))
retracted_reason: False national zero: inferred only from Uganda's absence from the WER 1983 annual notification table (the same method the prior audit retracted for 1981, 1984-86, 1988-90 and 1993); contradicted by Nairobi radio 30 Apr 1983 (19 cholera patients admitted from Uganda during the Busia border-town epidemic, new row 290, source 187) and by Radio Uganda 8 Jan 1984 (cholera outbreak on the NE shore of Lake Albert had already killed 10, source 188). WHO had carried eight Ugandan districts on its cholera infected-areas list until the day before this row began (24 Mar 1983).
